full_judgment:
"80. Presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence-when even any document is produced before any Court, purporting to be a record or memorandum of the evidence, or of any part of the evidence, given by a witness in a judicial proceeding or before any officer authorised by law to take such evidence or to be a statement or confession by any prisoner or accused person, taken in accordance with law, and purporting to be signed by any judge or Magistrate, or by any such officer as aforesaid, the Court shall presume that the document is genuine; that any statement as to the circumstances under which it was taken, purporting to be made by the person signing it, are true, and that such evidence, statement or confession was duly taken." 

 10. From the above, we find that section 80 relates to presumption as to documents produced as record of evidence. The section itself does not deal with the admissibility of the evidence of statements as referred to in the section but deals with presumption as to such documents. Only about two classes of documents, presumption can be made under this section, (1) documents purporting to be the record of the evidence of a witness giving in a judicial proceeding and (II), documents purported to be the record of the statement or confession made by a prisoner or accused persons. 

 11. From the deposition of the investigating officer, PW 5, we find that statement of the victim was recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure during investigation stage. But the presumption under section 80 of the Evidence Act can be made if such evidence is given in a judicial proceeding. In the instant case, the evidence recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure is not the evidence of a witness recorded in a judicial proceeding. Evidence given by witness during investigation cannot be considered as evidence given in a judicial proceeding as provided in section 80 of the Evidence Act. So, we are of the view that the High Court Division wrongly applied the provisions of section 80 to admit into evidence a statement of a witness recorded under section 164 during investigation stage and not in a judicial proceeding. Moreover, it is now a settled principle of law that statement recorded under section 164 can be used against the maker by the prosecution to corroborate the statement of the maker and by the defence for contradiction. In the instant case, the maker i.e., the victim while deposing as PW 6 before the Court did not support the prosecution case, she was cross-examined on behalf of the prosecution by declaring her hostile but the prosecution did not bring it to her notice the statement which was recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. Moreover, no explanation was given as to why the Magistrate who recorded the statement of the victim under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure was not produced before the tribunal for examination. For all these reasons, there was no scope of placing reliance upon the above statement recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
